name: DayDreamer
summary: DayDreamer runs Dreamer directly on four physical robots, learning a world model online from real experience and training the policy inside imagination so that real interaction is used with maximum efficiency. A quadruped learned to walk in about an hour of real time, and robot arms learned visual pick-and-place, all without simulators or resets engineered per task.
innovation: Demonstrated online world-model learning is fast enough for real hardware timescales.
Removed the simulator from the loop entirely, and with it the sim-to-real gap.
matters: The strongest evidence that dreaming is a practical real-robot method rather than a benchmark artifact.
limits: Single-task, low-dimensional settings; nothing like VLA-level semantic generality.
lineage: Dreamer deployed directly on physical robots with online model learning.
